beats.title: Intro: Brackets Are a Rectangle
beats.says: Why does x plus 3, times x plus 2, give x squared plus 5x plus 6? Most people just learn the rule. But draw it as a rectangle, and it's obvious. Then factorising is the same picture, backwards.

beats.title: The Picture: Area of a Rectangle
beats.says: A rectangle's area is width times height. Make the width x plus 3, and the height x plus 2. Now split it into four parts. x times x is x squared. x times 3 is 3x. 2 times x is 2x. And 2 times 3 is 6. Add them together: x squared plus 5x plus 6.
beats.key: Expanding = finding the area: multiply every part by every part.

beats.title: The Method: With a Negative
beats.says: Negatives work the same way, you just keep the signs. x plus 4, times x minus 1. x times x is x squared. 4 times x is 4x. Minus 1 times x is minus x. And 4 times minus 1 is minus 4. Collect the x terms: x squared plus 3x minus 4.

beats.title: Factorising: The Rectangle Backwards
beats.says: Factorising goes backwards. Start with x squared plus 5x plus 6. Put the x squared in one corner and the 6 in the other. The two side numbers have to multiply to 6, and add to 5 for the middle. That's 2 and 3, so the brackets are x plus 2, times x plus 3.
beats.key: Factorising: find two numbers that multiply to the last number and add to the middle one.

beats.title: Finding the Two Numbers
beats.says: To find them, list the pairs that multiply to 6. 1 and 6 add to 7: no. 2 and 3 add to 5: that works. So it's x plus 2, times x plus 3.

beats.title: Negative Numbers
beats.says: Now x squared plus 2x minus 15. The numbers multiply to minus 15, so one must be negative. 1 and minus 15 add to minus 14. Minus 1 and 15 add to 14. 3 and minus 5 add to minus 2. Minus 3 and 5 add to 2: that works. So it's x minus 3, times x plus 5.
beats.key: Last number negative? One number is negative, one positive.

beats.title: Always Check
beats.says: Always check by expanding back out. x minus 3, times x plus 5: x squared, plus 5x, minus 3x, minus 15. That's x squared plus 2x minus 15. It matches.
beats.onScreen: Worked: (x − 3)(x + 5) // expand to check | x² + 5x − 3x − 15 | x² + 2x − 15 ✓ // matches the question

beats.title: Solving: Make It Equal Zero
beats.says: Factorising lets you solve quadratics. x squared plus 5x plus 6 equals 0 becomes x plus 2, times x plus 3, equals 0. If two things multiply to make 0, one of them must be 0. So x is minus 2, or x is minus 3.
beats.onScreen: Worked: x² + 5x + 6 = 0 | (x + 2)(x + 3) = 0 // factorise first | x + 2 = 0 or x + 3 = 0 // one bracket must be 0 | x = −2 or x = −3
beats.key: Solving: factorise, set each bracket to 0, flip the sign.

beats.title: Exam Tips: Common Mistakes
beats.says: The mistakes that lose marks: only multiplying the first terms and the last terms, losing a minus sign, picking numbers that multiply but don't add, and forgetting to flip the signs when solving.
beats.onScreen: Worked: ✗ (x + 3)(x + 2) = x² + 6 // multiply every part | ✗ 2 and 3 for x² + 6x + 6 // they must ADD to 6 too | ✗ (x + 2) = 0 → x = 2 // it's x = −2 | ✓ expand · pair · check · solve

beats.title: Your Turn: Question
beats.says: Your turn. Factorise x squared plus 7x plus 12. Pause the video and try it.
beats.onScreen: Your turn: question card with a countdown. Q: Factorise x² + 7x + 12.
beats.question: Factorise x² + 7x + 12

beats.title: Your Turn: Answer
beats.says: We need two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7. That's 3 and 4. So it's x plus 3, times x plus 4. If you got that, you've got it.
beats.question: Factorise x² + 7x + 12
